entries.subject: DLR Dawn HAMO natural color
entries.finding: The retained HAMO natural-color label was inspected: 26704×13080 samples, three byte bands, planetocentric simple-cylindrical mapping, east-positive longitude and center longitude 180°. Its 255 km projection sphere is not the mesh’s measured physical radius. The selected publisher color remains photometrically corrected 650/550/430 nm imagery with its recorded clipping and registration limitations; no new browser qualification was performed by reading the label.

entries.subject: DLR HAMO corrected monochrome
entries.finding: DLR HAMO corrected monochrome — Complementary candidate, excluded from this selection: natural color supplies the same broad surface interpretation; a separate grayscale view would duplicate it.
entries.revisitWhen: A changed source release adds independently useful geometry or metadata beyond the selected model; compare it before changing the displayed source.

entries.subject: DLR HAMO Clementine ratios
entries.finding: [DLR HAMO Clementine ratios](https://dawngis.dlr.de/data/Vesta/mosaics/HAMO/clementine/Vesta_clementine_HAMO-1-2_global.jp2) — Included from the publisher's original PDS ZIP. The three byte planes preserve the published 26,703 × 13,351 Clementine-style ratio composite. JP2 decoding is unnecessary. Ratios emphasize spectral differences, not mineral abundance.

entries.subject: DLR Dawn HAMO 64 ppd terrain

entries.subject: Versioned Vesta test and browser evidence
entries.finding: Lack of dated evidence was the baseline finding. The LAMO update now has focused qualification at 86364a47f5ab7261a3716897b5e421e81abf5458: three Vesta source/package checks, six projected-image checks and strict preparation types pass. Headless DPR 1/2 checks retain one scene and 800 faces through drag with the same photographic atlas and shadows off. All prior runtime image hashes and draw/hit geometry match the main baseline. New runtime downloads were fetched from their published hash URLs and verified. Evidence is retained beside the body in evidence/lamo-2026-09-14.json; this is not an aggregate build or independent camera-registration result.

entries.subject: DLR Dawn LAMO clear-filter global photographic mosaic
entries.finding: Retrieved the original global 8-bit PNG (80,112 × 40,056) and inspected the companion attached PDS label using a bounded archive range. This is a different observation product from the already selected HAMO color composite and the excluded corrected HAMO grayscale candidate: it retains low-altitude crater and trough photography with source illumination. The label supplies the planetocentric, positive-east Claudia grid, 255 km map radius, 20 m/pixel spacing and fractional pixel offsets. The prepared 8192 × 4096 map and fixed 800-face atlas have coarser display resolution. Exact-black fill is a heuristic because the publisher supplies no independent validity mask; gaps and seams remain visible. Full PDS pixels were not downloaded or compared against the PNG; only the original PNG is the selected photographic input.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a measurement of the observer-camera route
entries.finding: Vesta is the one body with both a survey of deconvolved SPHERE frames and a mapped surface, so its 30 camera-1 frames from 2018 (May 20, June 8 and July 10) are pinned not as a texture source but as a test of the route that photographs Kleopatra, Ausonia, Psyche, Sylvia and Kalliope. Each frame is cast through the shipped HAMO terrain with the camera the route derives from the pinned Dawn pole model (dawn_vesta_v04.tpc: Claudia system, W0 75.39) and pinned Horizons rows at the exposure midpoint, and its correlation with the Dawn colour mosaic is swept over a turn about the pole and over both mirrors. Measured over 30 frames with the limb-fitted centre: the peak sits at +0.5 degrees (median; mean +0.3), 28 of 30 within 3 degrees and all within 5; the model beats the better mirror by 2.5 times (median; 28 of 30 above 1.5). One pixel of disc centre is about one degree of longitude on these 170 to 190 pixel discs, so the residual is at the level of the centre measurement. With the IAU 2015 pole model from pck00011 (W0 285.39) instead, the same frames peak 210 degrees away, the stated distance between the two prime meridians: a kernel in the wrong longitude system is caught here, and by no silhouette. The exposure epoch is the midpoint of the 81 s exposure; using the start moves every peak by 0.75 degrees, which is why the five photographed bodies now state midpoint epochs. No SPHERE lens is prepared for Vesta: the Dawn mosaics are the surface.

entries.subject: DLR Dawn HAMO-1-2 clear-filter global mosaic (60 m/pixel, May 2013)
entries.finding: The only Dawn product that photographs Vesta's north pole: HAMO-2 (June to July 2012) imaged the northern hemisphere under low northern-spring sun after LAMO and the color HAMO mosaics had left it dark. Measured on the released PNG, the LAMO clear mosaic covers 84 % of the map and none of the band above 75° N; the HAMO-1-2 clear mosaic covers every band, with the 90–75° N band dim (mean 7 of 255) but photographed. It is added as the HAMO photography lens and as the fallback base of the natural-color and LAMO lenses.
